clue.text: Official statement that's loaded?.

definitions.meaning: a formal public announcement or news report
read playfully, a gun that is loaded has a ... it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an official pronouncement is a loaded, biased one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' suggests a biased statement, but the second reading is a gun with a BULLET IN it.
explanation.definitionFit: A news bulletin is a short official announcement; split in two, the word describes a charged firearm.

clue.text: Dog taken by Darwin on long voyage

definitions.meaning: a small hound used in hunting

definitions.text: taken by Darwin on long voyage
definitions.meaning: The ship on which Darwin sailed round the world

explanation.surface: Darwin brought a dog with him on his great voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pet on board, but the second sense is the ship itself.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a hunting hound breed and the name of the survey ship carrying Darwin.

clue.text: Setting for a cello composition

indicators.note: a composition puts parts together, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A place is found for a piece written for the cello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges A CELLO into LOCALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A locale is the place or scene where events happen.

clue.text: It's not hard to get behind on

definitions.text: It's not hard to get behind on

parts.words: It's not hard to get behind on
parts.note: something that is not hard which you sit your behind on: a comfortable upholstered seat

explanation.surface: Someone says it is simple to fall behind with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get behind on' reads like falling behind, but means putting your behind on a soft seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A comfortable armchair is soft rather than hard, and one sits on it.

clue.text: Breach of convention typical of Baker Street gang

definitions.meaning: a departure from the rules or normal practice
the Baker Street Irregulars were the street urchins who helped Sherlock Holmes

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour is said to be just like a London street gang's.
explanation.walkthrough: The Baker Street Irregulars were Sherlock Holmes's band of street boys; the second reading treats the word as the quality belonging to them.
explanation.definitionFit: An irregularity is a deviation from rule; playfully, it is also the quality of Holmes's Irregulars.

clue.text: Christmas or Easter, for example .

parts.note: these look like festivals, but both are places in the sea: Christmas in the Indian Ocean, Easter in the Pacific

explanation.surface: Two church festivals are offered as examples of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The festivals are a false trail: Christmas and Easter are both names of remote pieces of land surrounded by ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas Island and Easter Island are both bits of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Channel received by listeners

definitions.meaning: a strait or inlet of the sea

explanation.surface: A broadcasting channel is picked up by its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests a TV or radio station, but it is a stretch of water such as Plymouth Sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow sea passage is so called, and so is anything that can be heard.

clue.text: Flying display tolerated

parts.note: to air something is to show it off
borne means put up with

explanation.surface: An aerobatic show was put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carried in the sky is in flight.

clue.text: Ambition and means to get access to the House.

parts.note: drive is determination or ambition
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: Ambition and the right methods are needed to get into Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the House' suggests the House of Commons, but it is simply a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A driveway is a private road leading up to a home.

clue.text: Descent or ascent after Poles switched trains

indicators.note: the poles are N and S, so these two letters in the word ascent change places

parts.note: RY, short for railway, stands for the trains that run on it

explanation.surface: Someone muses on going down or up once the poles have been switched round on a railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are N and S, the compass poles; 'switched' swaps them in the word ascent, giving ANCEST. 'trains' as railway is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry is one's line of descent, the family lineage running back through forebears.

clue.text: Venetian artist has to watch one in Rome

parts.note: to watch over is to guard
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Venetian painter has to keep an eye on someone in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Francesco Guardi was an 18th-century painter of Venetian views.
explanation.definitionFit: Francesco Guardi was a painter from Venice famous for his cityscapes.

clue.text: Spears joint, showing the party spirit

parts.note: a partisan is a long-handled spear with a broad blade
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: Spears joined together show a festive mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party spirit' sounds festive, but means loyalty to a political faction.
explanation.definitionFit: Partisanship is strong loyalty to one faction or cause.

clue.text: Shrub I. planted in course of return visit

indicators.note: planted in the course of something means set inside it
a return visit goes back the way it came, so the word for visit is read backwards

parts.note: to pay a call is to visit

explanation.surface: During a return visit, the speaker put a shrub in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns CALL into LLAC, and 'planted in course of' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a flowering bush with fragrant purple or white blooms.

clue.text: Pretentious and badly organised

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something is both showy and poorly arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges ORGANISED into GRANDIOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiose describes something pompous and showy, aiming at more grandeur than it has.

clue.text: Dance craze

parts.note: not a fashionable new step, but a passionate obsession with one classical stage art

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a fashionable new dance, but it is an enthusiasm for ballet; the word is BALLET + O + MANIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Balletomania is an extreme enthusiasm for ballet, a mania for that stage art.

clue.text: Political statement clear on nothing

parts.note: manifest means plain or obvious
O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A policy speech is declared to be clear about nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a published declaration of a party's aims.

clue.text: Made mad 'atter pay for this entertainment?

indicators.note: letters driven mad are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland is made to pay for his famous celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made mad' rearranges 'ATTER PAY into TEAPARTY, the Mad Hatter's own gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea party is a social gathering, the Hatter's being the famous one in Wonderland.

clue.text: A remover of coats — or more?

definitions.text: A remover of coats — or more?

parts.words: A remover of coats — or more?
parts.note: a solvent removes coats of paint, and a performer may take off more than coats

explanation.surface: Someone or something strips off coats, perhaps more.
explanation.walkthrough: First read as a paint solvent; the 'or more?' hints at a striptease performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint-remover takes off layers of paint, while a striptease artist sheds clothing.

clue.text: Having initiative to start applying force

parts.note: to enter on something is to start it
prising is forcing something open with leverage

explanation.surface: Someone shows initiative by using force from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprising person is resourceful and ready to undertake new ventures.

clue.text: Rascal takes one sort of seafood

parts.note: a scamp is a mischievous rascal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rogue helps himself to some seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are breaded langoustine tails, a popular fried shellfish dish.

clue.text: He had a name as an author in his country

definitions.text: He had a name as an author
definitions.meaning: Anatole ... was a French Nobel-winning novelist who wrote under this name

explanation.surface: A writer was famous in his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: Anatole France took his country's name as his pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatole France was a famous novelist's pen name, and the same word names the nation he came from.

clue.text: University with a royal style

parts.note: a prince is a member of a royal family
ton is fashionable style

explanation.surface: A college is described as having regal flair.
explanation.walkthrough: TON is an old word for fashion or high style.
explanation.definitionFit: Princeton is an Ivy League institution in New Jersey.

clue.text: General of note, as it happens

parts.note: C is a musical note
a live broadcast is shown as it happens

explanation.surface: A distinguished general, it turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Clive was the British general of the 18th century known as Clive of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Clive of India was a British military commander in eighteenth-century India.

clue.text: .To.oppose king could be a problem

parts.note: to face an opponent is to confront them
R stands for king, from the Latin rex

explanation.surface: Standing up to the monarch might cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A facer is an old term for a sudden difficulty, originally a blow to the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A facer is a sudden setback or difficulty that confronts one head-on.

clue.text: Go right

definitions.meaning: to ... to a place is to go there
to right something is to fix it

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to betake oneself somewhere; the other is to mend or put back in order.

clue.text: Duchess managed to conceal queen, perhaps

indicators.note: the words conceal the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: A duchess managed to keep the queen's identity secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to conceal' points to CHESSMAN within DuCHESS MANaged; the queen is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is one example of a piece used on the chessboard.

clue.text: Ball in royal house with monarch present

parts.note: York was an English royal dynasty
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the reigning monarch when this was set

explanation.surface: A dance is held at the palace with the queen attending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball' suggests a dance, but it is a cricket delivery: a yorker is pitched right at the batsman's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A yorker is a cricket delivery aimed to land at the batsman's toes.

clue.text: Becoming a quiet river location

parts.note: P stands for piano, quiet in music
the Po is the great river of northern Italy
a site is a location

explanation.surface: A peaceful riverside spot is described as attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' means suitable or fitting, not changing into something.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming here means fitting or suitable, and apposite means appropriate to the occasion.
